status_summary: H.R. 1468, introduced 2025-02-21, would establish a CCP Initiative in the Justice Department's National Security Division to counter Chinese government espionage, trade secret theft and critical infrastructure threats, which the CRS summary describes as reestablishing the initiative discontinued in 2022; the House Judiciary Committee reported it as H. Rept. 119-699 and it was placed on the Union Calendar on 2026-06-15, and the Senate companion S. 672 remains in committee. Earlier, the House Appropriations Committee's fiscal year 2026 Commerce, Justice, Science summary, updated 2025-07-23, listed directing the re-establishment of the initiative, but press reports in January 2026 said the language was removed before the act was enacted as Public Law 119-74 on 2026-01-23. No Justice Department announcement or directive restarting the initiative was found.

timeline.event: H.R. 1468, which would establish a CCP Initiative in the Justice Department's National Security Division, is introduced in the House and referred to the Judiciary Committee.
The House Appropriations Committee's summary of its fiscal year 2026 Commerce, Justice, Science bill listed directing the re-establishment of the DOJ China Initiative.

The Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 was enacted as Public Law 119-74; press reports said the China Initiative language had been removed before final passage.
The House Judiciary Committee reports H.R. 1468 as amended (H. Rept. 119-699), and it is placed on the Union Calendar as No. 607.

title: Restart the DOJ China Initiative
uncertainties: Checked systematically on 2026-10-18. (1) Federal Register API: queries on China Initiative returned no documents since 2025-01-20, and a National Security Division with China variant returned only unrelated documents. (2) Unified Agenda: item listings could not be reached and the Federal Register fallback was used. (3) congress.gov and govinfo: H.R. 1468 would set up a CCP Initiative in the Justice Department's National Security Division, which the CRS summary describes as reestablishing the 2018 to 2022 effort; it was reported by the House Judiciary Committee and placed on the Union Calendar on 2026-06-15 and has not passed the House, and the Senate companion S. 672 has had no action since referral on 2025-02-20. The reported bill text has no public education provision and does not name the former China Initiative. (4) Agency pages: the National Security Division page showed individual cases and no program announcement. (5) News: one search returned coverage of the dropped appropriations proposal. The House FY2026 committee report directive and its removal before Public Law 119-74 rest on a members' letter and two secondary sources, one from an advocacy group; the committee report and final explanatory statement were not opened. The 2025-02-05 closure of the Foreign Influence Task Force concerns foreign-influence work and is not a restart. A full search of Justice Department press releases was not done.
